info.title: Pepo API
info.summary: A growing library of public social video, analyzed once and asked many times, as an API and an MCP server.
info.description:
Pepo keeps a library of public TikTok and Instagram video, plus public Reddit threads, for each workspace. Every video is analyzed once when it arrives: a timed transcript, a record of what is on screen, and a summary of what the creator says and how they feel about it. After that the library can be searched, counted and questioned as often as needed, from your own code or from an agent in Claude or ChatGPT through the MCP server, which is a client of this API.

Two jobs it is built for: a consumer brand reading what people see, say and feel about it and its competitors, and a creator learning what works in a niche.

This spec documents **only endpoints that are live today**. Anything specified but not shipped is absent rather than documented ahead of itself: a documented endpoint that 404s costs more trust than a short reference.

Two properties run through every response and are worth reading before the endpoint list:

1. **Reliability travels in the payload.** Scores ship with the confidence, observation coverage and comparison group behind them, and with `floors_met` stating whether the evidence bar for the claim was actually cleared. The primary consumer of this API is a language model, and a model handed a bare number will restate it as a fact.
2. **Refusals are results.** When the evidence does not support a claim, the API says so in a field rather than returning a confident number. A video with two observations is `watchlist` with a `gated_by` explanation, no matter how large its view count, and a question no video could answer comes back as `answer: null` with a `reason`.

Views are observed content views, never ad impressions. A brand's own posts are never counted as signal. Nothing here measures paid media, sales or audience demographics.

get.description: Free access to stored public comments in the workspace selected by the API key. Text is verbatim. Tone is a derived comment classification, not video sentiment or a count of distinct people. Quality counts describe this page only. Pages are limited by row count and bytes read; continue with `next_cursor` until `has_more` is false before claiming whole-library coverage. A short page is not proof of completion.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque continuation cursor from this workspace's previous comment page. Omit to restart.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum requested rows. The server may return fewer at its read-size boundary.

200.description: One comment page with coverage and continuation state.

url.description: Recovered HTTP(S) parent source URL, or null when unavailable.

400.description: Invalid `limit`, or a cursor this query cannot read. Restart pagination without a cursor when it is rejected.

get.description: Current prepaid balance for the workspace the key belongs to, and the default per-call cost ceiling. Free: this endpoint never meters.

200.description: Current balance.

default_call_cap_usd.description: Workspace-level override of the per-endpoint default ceiling. `null` means the per-endpoint default applies.

mode.description: What this key is allowed to do. `live` meters real credits and can start collection. `test` does neither: it reads this workspace's own corpus, unmetered and read-only, so an integration can be exercised without spending. The token's prefix states the mode (`pk_live_` / `pk_test_`). Whether a response is labelled sample data comes from the workspace, not this field.

post.summary: Estimate the cost of a call
post.description:
What a call would cost, as a low/expected/high band with the assumptions behind it, including how many stored posts the call would read.

Free, and deliberately prominent. An agent that can price its own plan proposes the affordable version first, which turns the per-call ceiling into something the caller cooperates with rather than collides with.

The endpoints listed in `endpoint` are priced from their own cost model. Any other value is not refused, but it is quoted as a flat single `search_request` that describes nothing real: `POST /v1/library/analyze` is priced by `library.estimated_cost_usd` on a `needs_analysis` answer instead, and `POST /v1/collections/preview` is always one `search_request`.

endpoint.description: Which call to price. `/v1/monitors` prices one run of `params.workflow` and adds `runs_per_month` and `monthly_expected_usd` to `assumes`, so `monthly_cap_usd` can be set from what a recurring job will actually reach. `/v1/library/add` prices `count` videos kept at one `post_collected` each.

params.description: The parameters you intend to send to that endpoint.

treatment.description: `/v1/collections` only: price collection plus the corpus run (`full`) or collection alone (`collect_only`).

target.description: `/v1/collections` and `collection_topup` monitors: posts to land per run.

workflow.description: `/v1/monitors` only: the workflow the monitor would run.

hits.description: `/v1/corpus/ask` only: how many videos may be read for the answer. `low` is the question alone; `expected` and `high` assume every hit is read live, so `hits` is also the price ceiling. Hits answered from the stored transcript, the cache or the stored analysis are not billed as reads.

window.description: Corpus-reading endpoints: the `window` you intend to send, so the post count matches the call.

subject.description: Accepted for readability; not used in the price.

200.description: Cost band and the assumptions behind it.

cost_usd.description: Low, expected and high are identical when the library could be counted in advance, which is the normal case for the corpus-reading endpoints. They widen when it could not, and for collections and `/v1/corpus/ask`.

assumes.description: Notably `posts_considered`, how many stored posts the call will read: that is what the price tracks, and what the invoice bills. For `/v1/monitors`, also `runs_per_month` (30 daily, 4.3 weekly) and `monthly_expected_usd`, the per-run band times the schedule.

get.description:
The approved brand profile for this workspace: products, competitors, category, audiences, official accounts, and the topics the brand refuses to be associated with. Every workflow reads it, so results are generic category noise until it exists.

A workspace without one gets `200` with `status: "needs_setup"` and the path to fix it, **not** a `404`. The empty state is the onboarding, and a caller that receives an error on its first call abandons the task.

200.description: The approved profile, or a setup instruction.

value.message: No brand profile yet. Every workflow reads it, so results are generic until it exists.

post.summary: Create or replace the brand profile
post.description:
Saves the profile and makes it active immediately. Every workflow result from then on records its version in `brand_profile_version`.

Call this before any workflow: they return `409 profile_required` until a profile exists, because results without one would be category noise rather than answers about your brand.

Replacing a profile creates a new version rather than mutating the old one; previous versions are retained.

brand_names.description: Required. Include spelling variants and nicknames: people rarely write your brand the way your style guide does.

judge_category.description: What counts as on-topic vs. noise when the corpus judge reads collected posts for this brand. Different from `category` (the industry label): this refines the judge's category definition. The judge never sees the brand name itself, so phrase `means`/`other` about the content, not the brand.

means.description: What on-topic content is for this brand, when judging collected posts.

other.description: What should be treated as noise, when judging collected posts.

exclusions.description: Topics withheld from every result, enforced server-side. Withheld rows are counted in `corpus.excluded_by_brand_profile` so the filtering is never silent.

handle.description: Normalized on save: lowercased, leading `@` stripped.

platform.description: Omit to match this handle on any platform.

owner.description: Must name an entry already in `brand_names` or `competitors`, or the entry rides back in `official_account_gaps`.

official_accounts.description: This brand's and its competitors' own accounts. A brand's own posts are never signal: posts from these accounts are withheld at read time from search, trending, share of voice, product and competitor results, and counted in `excluded_official`.

lens.description: The industry vocabulary every report uses for "product", "competitor", "SKU" and "consumer". Inferred from `category` when omitted.

official_account_gaps.description: One message per `official_accounts` entry whose `owner` matches neither `brand_names` nor `competitors` in the request body just saved.

post.summary: Find trending videos
post.description:
Ranked videos with a momentum score, a classification, and the evidence behind both.

**A video is not trending because it has many views.** Each result is ranked as a percentile within a comparison group (same platform, comparable creators) and against the creator's own baseline, and a classification above `watchlist` requires at least **3 metric snapshots across at least 12 hours**. Anything thinner is capped at `watchlist` with `gated_by` explaining why, including videos with very large view counts.

The trend-level verdict is reported separately from the per-video ranking, because one video outperforming is virality, not a movement.

Costs credits: one `search_request` plus one `content_enriched` per stored post read. Price it first with `POST /v1/estimate`.

platforms.description: Omit for every platform in the corpus.

window.description: How far back to look, e.g. `24h`, `7d`, `30d`. `all`, or omitting it, reads all time, newest first. An unparseable value is a 400; it is never silently widened.

max_cost_usd.description: Ceiling on the charge for this call. The work always runs to completion; the charge is held at the smaller of the estimate and this ceiling, and `usage.charge_capped` says when the metered cost went above it. Results are complete either way. A server default applies when omitted.

200.description: Ranked results with their evidence.

post.summary: Compare share of voice against competitors
post.description:
Share of observed views between this brand and its configured competitors, over the library already collected.

**This is not ad impressions.** Views are observed content views; an impression is an ad-delivery event. The two are not interchangeable and this response must never be presented as impression share.

**Check `reliability` before quoting a percentage.** A library collected by searching for your own brand cannot measure your share of it: you dominate it by construction. The endpoint derives how the library was gathered from the collection runs behind it (`corpus_origin`) and refuses to endorse a split it cannot support, returning the numbers alongside the reason they should not be quoted.

Organic and paid activity are not separated: nothing in the library records whether a post was promoted.

Costs credits: one `search_request` plus one `content_enriched` per stored post read. Price it first with `POST /v1/estimate`.

platforms.description: Omit for every platform in the corpus.

window.description: How far back to look, e.g. `7d`, `30d`, or `all`. Omitted reads all time, newest first.

max_cost_usd.description: Ceiling on the charge for this call. The work always runs to completion; the charge is held at the smaller of the estimate and this ceiling, and `usage.charge_capped` says when the metered cost went above it. Results are complete either way. A server default applies when omitted.

200.description: The split, and whether it can be quoted.

post.summary: Report on what a competitor changed
post.description:
What changed for a competitor between the last two equal-length periods, decomposed into the creators, videos or platforms that caused it, with an annotated attention timeline naming the videos behind each peak.

**The breakdown reconciles or it is not shown.** A waterfall's whole visual claim is "here is the change, and here is what it was made of", so the parts must sum to the whole exactly, including after truncation, which produces an explicit remainder row rather than dropping the tail. `reconciles` is computed, not assumed.

**Check `comparable` first.** A period-over-period comparison across an unevenly collected library measures the collection, not the market: a competitor 'gaining' between two windows may only mean we searched harder the second time.

Comparative product and SKU bars are **not available**: the profile holds no competitor SKUs and nothing resolves a caption to a competitor's product line, so ranking them would mean inventing the categories. This is stated in `unavailable` rather than omitted.

Costs credits: one `search_request` plus one `content_enriched` per stored post read across both periods. Price it first with `POST /v1/estimate`.

competitor.description: Which competitor. Omit for the one with the most video in the window.

window.description: Length of EACH period. The prior period of equal length is the baseline.

dimension.description: How to break down the change. Defaults to creator.

max_cost_usd.description: Ceiling on the charge for this call. The work always runs to completion; the charge is held at the smaller of the estimate and this ceiling, and `usage.charge_capped` says when the metered cost went above it. Results are complete either way. A server default applies when omitted.

200.description: What changed, what caused it, and whether it can be read as movement.

post.summary: What people say about a product or SKU
post.description:
Purchase drivers, complaints, needs and use cases for this brand's products, drawn from the captions and comments of posts that name a product.

**Scope: this brand's own catalog only.** A competitor's product or brand is out of scope here; use `POST /v1/competitors/report` instead. A `sku` that names none of this brand's own catalog products comes back as `unknown_sku: true`, an input error rather than an empty finding.

**A theme mentioned twice is not a finding.** Themes below three distinct sources or two distinct voices are returned in `seen_not_established` rather than in `findings`: visible and countable, but never rankable. A two-mention theme rendered as a bar reads as a product problem, and that is the specific mistake this split exists to prevent.

**Quotes are verbatim.** Every finding carries the exact text and the id it came from, because a finding whose evidence is a paraphrase cannot be checked.

**Count voices, not mentions.** Five comments from one account is one person; `voices` is reported alongside `sources` so a single loud detractor cannot become "a widely reported issue".

Themes are multi-label ("love the texture but it broke me out" is a driver and a complaint), so counts deliberately do not sum to `sources_considered`.

Reddit, retailer reviews and timestamped video evidence are **absent, not thin**, and say so in `unavailable`.

Costs credits: one `search_request` plus one `content_enriched` per source read. Price it first with `POST /v1/estimate`.

sku.description: Narrow to one or more of this brand's own catalog products. An exact catalog name matches just that product; a generic term ("knee sleeve") matches every product whose name, line or variants contain those words, and the matched product(s) come back in `resolved_skus`. Not a competitor's product or brand: those belong on `POST /v1/competitors/report` instead. Omit for all configured products.

max_cost_usd.description: Ceiling on the charge for this call. The work always runs to completion; the charge is held at the smaller of the estimate and this ceiling, and `usage.charge_capped` says when the metered cost went above it. Results are complete either way. A server default applies when omitted.

200.description: Themes with their evidence, and what was not established.

post.summary: Find creators for a product, topic or audience
post.description:
Creators in this brand's library with median views, median engagement, best post, consistency, the competitors they also post about, and brand-safety flags.

**Medians, not averages.** One 486K video against nine 3K videos averages to 51K, which describes none of the ten and flatters the creator enormously. `bestViews` is reported alongside so a one-hit creator is visible as one.

**A creator with one post is not ranked.** One post has no median and no dispersion; those creators come back in `single_post_creators`, present and countable but never comparable with the ranked list.

**Post count is a fact about our search.** Creators are here because their posts matched what was collected, so `postsInCorpus` is never their output.

**A brand-safety flag is a hit, never a clearance.** Screening is keyword-based over captions only: it cannot see video content, audio, or posts outside this library. Zero flags means nothing matched, not that a creator is safe, and `safety_statement` must travel with any safety claim.

Follower counts, demographics and audience overlap are not collected, so nothing here says whether a creator's audience is yours. Observed views are not reach.

Costs credits: one `search_request` plus one `content_enriched` per stored post read. Price it first with `POST /v1/estimate`.

sku.description: Creators who posted about this product. Must be a product name from the profile, not the brand name.

topic.description: Creators whose captions mention this term.

max_cost_usd.description: Ceiling on the charge for this call. The work always runs to completion; the charge is held at the smaller of the estimate and this ceiling, and `usage.charge_capped` says when the metered cost went above it. Results are complete either way. A server default applies when omitted.

200.description: Ranked creators, those seen once, and what was not screened.

post.summary: Measure social response to a campaign or launch
post.description:
What happened around a campaign or product launch: an annotated timeline, a reconciling contribution waterfall by SKU, creator, video or platform, and an ownership split, over equal-length windows either side of the launch.

**This is not paid-owned-earned; it is owned versus not-owned.** Owned is derivable, because a post from a connected account is the brand's. Paid versus earned is not derivable from anything: a sponsored creator post and an organic fan post are identical in this library. Caption-based `#ad` detection was considered and rejected: disclosure is inconsistent, and treating its absence as evidence of organic reach would be worse than having no split. Two buckets that are true beat three where one is invented.

**It is not causal.** There is no control group and no counterfactual. Anything rising for an unrelated reason rises here too, so this describes what happened around the launch, not what the launch caused.

**Response by market is unavailable**: posts carry no country, region or language. The markets on the brand profile describe who the brand sells to, not where a viewer was.

Equal-length windows are used on both sides deliberately: comparing "since launch" against "everything before" makes the lift depend on how far back the library happens to reach.

Costs credits: one `search_request` plus one `content_enriched` per stored post read across both windows. Price it first with `POST /v1/estimate`.

launch_at.description: Launch time, unix ms. Defaults to one window ago.

window.description: Length of EACH side of the launch.

term.description: Narrow to captions containing this term, e.g. a campaign hashtag.

max_cost_usd.description: Ceiling on the charge for this call. The work always runs to completion; the charge is held at the smaller of the estimate and this ceiling, and `usage.charge_capped` says when the metered cost went above it. Results are complete either way. A server default applies when omitted.

200.description: What moved around the launch, and what cannot be said about it.

post.summary: Search the video library
post.description:
Find videos in this workspace's library by topic, product or creator.

**Read `search_method` on every response.** This matches words in stored captions, creator handles, each video's stored analysis (summary, hook, themes, claims) when one has been run, and reviewed pilot identity evidence when present. Timed transcripts, the on-screen record and audio are not searched here (ask about those with `POST /v1/corpus/ask`), so an empty result means *not found in what is searchable*, never *no such video exists*. That distinction matters if you are about to report that a topic has no coverage.

Costs credits: one `search_request` plus one `content_enriched` per stored post read.

window.description: How far back to look, e.g. `24h`, `7d`, `30d`. `all`, or omitting it, reads all time, newest first. An unparseable value is a 400; it is never silently widened.

max_cost_usd.description: Ceiling on the charge for this call. The work always runs to completion; the charge is held at the smaller of the estimate and this ceiling, and `usage.charge_capped` says when the metered cost went above it. Results are complete either way. A server default applies when omitted.

200.description: Matching videos, with a statement of what was actually searched.

post.summary: Ask a question of the analyzed videos
post.description:
Answer a natural-language question from what the videos in this workspace actually SAY and SHOW, with a citation (creator, URL, clip timestamps) under every paragraph. This is the brainstorming surface: ask "what do people complain about", "how do the videos that show the product differ from the ones that don't", or "which hooks recur", and follow up.

Retrieval is a search over the workspace's video index, re-ranked with the stored analyses; each of the top `hits` videos is then answered from its stored timed transcript and on-screen record first, and read live from the footage only when that text cannot answer. When a live read fails (asset gone, provider quota, time budget) the stored analysis stands in and `sources[].method` says so. When two or more videos are cited, `across_videos` counts their sentiment, format, setting, products and visible actions so a comparison rests on numbers.

**`answer: null` is a 200, not an error.** Before anything is searched or held, every video in the library (inside `window`, when given) must be analyzed: otherwise the answer is `reason: "needs_analysis"` with the count and price of catching up, unbilled, and `POST /v1/library/analyze` starts it. `no_index` means nothing has been indexed yet (unbilled). `no_hits` means no indexed video matched within the window: *not in the analyzed videos*, never *nobody said it*. `unsupported_question` means the question itself (audience demographics, sales or revenue, ad spend, or whether something is trending now) is not something any video could ever answer, decided before the index is checked, unbilled. Only one video per duplicate cluster is indexed, so `index_videos` is smaller than the library.

Costs credits: one `corpus_question` per question answered (including `no_hits`), plus one `video_read` per video whose footage was read live for this ask. Answers from the stored transcript or on-screen record (`read_transcript`), from the answer cache (`cached: true`), from stored analysis, or unanswered are not reads and are not billed. Nothing is billed for `needs_analysis`, `no_index`, `unsupported_question`, or a result where every hit degraded and no footage was read live.

question.description: The question, in plain language, e.g. "what do founders say about fundraising?"

hits.description: How many top-ranked videos are answered. Also the price ceiling: at most one `video_read` per hit, billed only for footage actually read live, on top of the `corpus_question`.

window.description: How far back to look, e.g. `24h`, `7d`, `30d`. `all`, or omitting it, reads all time, newest first. An unparseable value is a 400; it is never silently widened.

max_cost_usd.description: Ceiling on the charge for this call. The work always runs to completion; the charge is held at the smaller of the estimate and this ceiling, and `usage.charge_capped` says when the metered cost went above it. Results are complete either way. A server default applies when omitted.

video_ids.description: Ask only these videos: the `post_id` of earlier citations, or ids from search or list results. A follow-up about the videos an answer cited stays on them instead of searching the whole library. Every named video that is analyzed is read, and `hits` defaults to how many were named. Only these videos have to be analyzed for the ask to proceed. An id that is not a video in this library is a `400` naming it.

libraries.description: `this` asks this workspace's library. `all` asks every Pepo library's analyzed videos, for when this one is thin on a subject: billed like any ask, not gated on this library's unanalyzed videos, and each citation carries `in_your_library`. `POST /v1/library/add` keeps the others at $0.02 each, with their analysis. Cannot be combined with `video_ids`.

value.question: what do founders say about raising a seed round?

200.description: The answer with citations, or `answer: null` with a `reason` when there is nothing to answer from.

get.summary: Questions the library could not answer
get.description:
Recent questions asked through `POST /v1/corpus/ask` and `POST /v1/search/videos`, grouped into thin or no coverage versus answered fine. `thin` is exactly what each handler already knew at response time, never a threshold recomputed here: an ask that returned a `reason` (`no_index`, `no_hits`, `unsupported_question`, `needs_analysis`, `analysis_running`), or a search that matched nothing (`empty_corpus` when the library itself was empty for the filters, `no_caption_match` when it was not). Each group carries its count, first and last asked timestamps, and up to 50 of the underlying questions with their own result count and reason.

Free. Use this to see what this workspace is asking that the library cannot answer, then close the gap: grow search terms with `POST /v1/monitors` (a new `collection_topup` schedule) or `POST /v1/monitors/{monitor_id}/update` (`add_subjects` on an existing one), or fix an on-category miss with `POST /v1/brand-profile` (`judge_category`, `hashtags`, `brand_names`). This endpoint only surfaces the gap; it never changes a schedule or a profile itself.

`truncated: true` means the scan hit its 2,000-row cap before covering the whole window; the counts are then a floor, not a total. Live keys only: the log contains verbatim questions from live users, so test keys receive `403 test_key_forbidden`, the one read endpoint test mode does not get.

parameters.name: window_days
parameters.description: How far back to look. Defaults to 30, capped at 90. Must be a positive number.

200.description: Recent questions, grouped by coverage.

scanned.description: Rows read from the window, up to the 2,000-row scan cap.

truncated.description: The scan hit its cap: there may be more questions in the window than these counts show.

403.description: Test key: this endpoint serves verbatim live-user question text and is refused in test mode (`test_key_forbidden`).

error.message: Test keys cannot read coverage gaps: the log contains verbatim questions from live users. Use a live key.

post.summary: Analyze the videos waiting in the library
post.description:
The yes to a `needs_analysis` answer from `POST /v1/corpus/ask`: analyzes the videos in the library that have not been analyzed yet, including rows a `collect_only` collection left waiting. Nothing new is collected. Reddit rows, excluded rows, the brand's own posts and the non-representative copies of a duplicate cluster are skipped: they were never part of what an ask reads.

**Price.** Each waiting video is priced for the steps it still needs: one `video_analyzed` ($0.125) if it has no stored analysis, one `video_indexed` ($0.10) for the search index, and one `content_enriched` ($0.002) for the media fetch. There is no subject check in a library pass. A video up to 3 minutes long is one unit of `video_analyzed` and `video_indexed`; past 3 minutes it is one more unit per started 72 seconds, so a long video costs more than a short clip rather than being sold below cost. A video of unknown length is priced as a short one (see `library.videos_of_unknown_length`). The estimate is held when the pass starts and settled once it finishes for the steps that actually ran, never above the hold.

**Passes.** One pass may hold at most the call cap: `max_cost_usd` when given, else the workspace's own default call cap, else the endpoint default. The pass takes the waiting videos that fit under it, in library order; `videos_left_for_a_later_pass` says how many remain, and the next ask quotes them. It is refused with `budget_too_low` only when not even one waiting video fits.

Returns 202 once accepted; poll `GET /v1/collections/{collection_id}` for progress, then ask the same question again through `POST /v1/corpus/ask` once it finishes. Returns 200 with `started: false` and no charge when nothing is waiting, or when a pass is already running for this brand, in which case `library.analysis_in_progress` names it.

max_cost_usd.description: Optional ceiling for this pass. The pass takes only the waiting videos whose estimated cost fits under it; if not even one fits, the call is refused with `budget_too_low` and nothing starts.

200.description: Nothing was started: either every analyzable video is already analyzed, or a pass is already running for this brand. Nothing was charged.

202.description: Accepted. The analysis run has started; it is not finished.

collection_id.description: The collection this pass runs under. Poll it with `GET /v1/collections/{collection_id}`.

collection.description: The same view `GET /v1/collections/{collection_id}` returns, so a client can draw the pass like any other collection.

videos_in_this_pass.description: Waiting videos this pass will analyze.

videos_left_for_a_later_pass.description: Waiting videos that did not fit under this pass's cap. Non-zero means another pass is needed once this one finishes.

400.description: Either `invalid_request` (an unknown field, or `max_cost_usd` is not a positive number) or `budget_too_low` (not even one waiting video fits under `max_cost_usd` or the call cap, or the workspace's own call cap holds less than this pass is estimated at). Nothing is started or charged either way.

capTooLow.summary: max_cost_usd below the cheapest waiting video

error.message: Analyzing even one of the 40 videos waiting in the library is estimated at $0.23, above the $0.10 this call may spend. Nothing was started.

500.description: The pass could not be opened or prepared. Anything held for it has been returned.

get.description:
Full detail for a single video: engagement, the metric history behind any momentum claim, a sample of comments with their tone **and the coverage of that tone**, the stored analysis of what the video says and shows (`analysis`), and the playable file when one was captured (`media`).

`media.video_url_kind` tells you what `media.video_url` is worth: `stored` is a durable copy that keeps playing, `cdn_signed` is a signed platform url that expires within hours of ingest: play it if it loads, but keep `video.thumb_url` and `video.url` as the fallback.

Use the coverage. A tone split computed over 3 classified comments of 1,840 sampled is not the same claim as one computed over 1,800, and the split alone cannot tell them apart. Free.

parameters.name: video_id
parameters.description: The `video.id` from a search or trending result.

200.description: The video, its observation history, and its comment reaction.

404.description: No video with that id in this workspace. Returned identically for an id that does not exist and one belonging to another workspace: the difference would be an existence oracle across tenants.

get.description: Cursor-paged rows of the library with a quality assessment. Free: these rows were already paid for at collection, and charging to read them would make careful paging the expensive option. Newest first by publish date. Rows the subject check excluded are withheld unless `include_excluded=true`. Use `evidence_status` to page one pilot evidence status without scanning unrelated rows; the filter is applied before pagination, and filtered page counts are not whole-library counts. `format=csv` returns `text/csv` instead of JSON. Each JSON row carries `sentiment`, the video's overall valence from its stored analysis (null when it has not been analyzed), so a caller can split a page by sentiment without calling `GET /v1/videos/{video_id}` per row.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque; pass back what the previous page returned.

parameters.name: evidence_status
parameters.description: Exact pilot evidence status, applied before pagination. Anything other than the five values is a 400. `rejected`, `conflicted` and `unknown` rows are ineligible, so they are withheld unless `include_excluded=true` is also set, for an audit.

parameters.name: include_excluded
parameters.description: Audit only. Include rows the subject check excluded (or pilot evidence marked ineligible). Returned rows say so in `judgeExcluded`. Only the exact value `true` turns it on.

200.description: A page of rows. With `format=csv`, the same rows as `text/csv`.

quality.description: Row count, platform mix, duplicates, per-field gaps with their consequence, real time span, stated limitations, a verification block distinguishing 'complete' from 'confirmed', and stacked composition. `composition.unavailable` names the axes with no data behind them (market has no geography anywhere in the library; category is a single brand-level value, so its bar would be one segment at 100%): report those as unavailable rather than as empty. Describes this page only.

400.description: `evidence_status` is not one of the five values.

post.summary: Preview what a subject would collect
post.description:
One provider search page per platform for `subject`, exactly the search `POST /v1/collections` would run, and nothing else: no row is written and no run is started. Call it before a collection whenever the subject is a person, band, product nickname or rare word. Keyword search on the platforms matches fuzzily, and a collection started on a bad match pays for collection and the subject check before finding out.

`mention_rate` is the share of returned posts whose caption names the subject, by the same rule the subject check uses, so a high rate here is the same signal a full collection would find. `verdict` reads it: `looks_right` at 0.6 or above, `mixed` at 0.25 or above, `looks_wrong` below that, and an empty page is `looks_wrong`. `suggestion` says what to try instead when it is not `looks_right`.

Takes the same `window` as `POST /v1/collections` (default `7d`): probe with the window you intend to collect with, since a rare subject checked against the default can come back legitimately empty.

Costs one `search_request` ($0.01), however many platforms are probed. Nothing is charged when the provider call fails. Live keys only.

subject.description: The search phrase to probe, as you would pass it to `POST /v1/collections`.

platforms.description: Defaults to both. Reddit is not accepted: its search does not fail in the fuzzy way this endpoint exists to catch.

window.description: How far back the probe looks, parsed exactly as `POST /v1/collections` parses it. Defaults to `7d`.

200.description: The page, how much of it names the subject, and what to do next.

502.description: The provider call failed. The message carries the provider's own error. The hold is released and nothing is charged.

post.summary: Start a collection run
post.description:
Starts an unattended job that searches a provider for `subject` and adds matching videos to this workspace's library. `budget_usd` is required: a collection spends provider credits unattended, so its ceiling is never optional. Price it first with `POST /v1/estimate` (`endpoint: "/v1/collections"`) and pass that estimate's `expected` cost as `budget_usd`. For a person, band or rare word, check what the provider actually returns first with `POST /v1/collections/preview`.

Returns 202: the run is accepted, not finished. Rows land as they are collected and are searchable immediately, flagged unverified until judged. Billing settles at the end for what actually landed, never for the estimate. Poll `GET /v1/collections/{collection_id}` for progress.

By default the run carries the **full treatment**: once collection ends, a corpus run checks each row is really about the subject, enriches metrics, clusters near-duplicates, analyzes and indexes each video (transcript, on-screen record, summary), and collects and reads about 20 comments per post. `budget_usd` must cover collection and treatment together (estimate with `treatment` set); the collection settles its own line and the corpus run settles once more, at the end, for the stages that actually ran. Pass `treatment: "collect_only"` for rows alone.

subject.description: The search phrase the provider collects for, e.g. "y combinator". One subject per run: start several runs for several subjects.

platforms.description: Defaults to tiktok and instagram (video). Add "reddit" for text posts and comment threads: reddit rows are checked for subject, de-duplicated, and have their comments collected and read, but are never watched or added to the video search index.

window.description: How far back to collect, e.g. "7d", "30d". Defaults to 7d.

target.description: How many videos to collect. Values outside 1 to 5000 are clamped.

budget_usd.description: Required hard ceiling for this run's spend.

treatment.description: What happens to the rows once they land. `full` (default) hands them to a corpus run (subject check, enrich, dedup, analyze, index, comments, comment sentiment), about $0.37 per landed post on top of collection's $0.02, billed only for the stages that actually run; its progress appears as `corpus_run` on the collection. `collect_only` stops at the rows ($0.02 per post), flagged unverified.

webhook_url.description: Optional, `https://` on a public host. With the full treatment, POSTed a `corpus_run.completed` event `{event, collection_id, corpus_run_id, status, cost_usd, stages, warnings}` when the corpus run finishes. Unsigned, best effort, one attempt with a 5s timeout, no retry.

full_treatment.summary: Collect 50 posts and run the full treatment

202.description: Accepted. The run has started; it is not finished.

400.description: Either `invalid_request` (a required field is missing or malformed, or an unknown field was sent) or `budget_too_low` (the estimated cost of this run is above `budget_usd`, or the workspace's default call cap holds less than the estimate; see BudgetTooLowError). Nothing is started or charged in either case.

error.message: budget_usd is required. A collection spends provider credits unattended, so its budget is not optional. Call POST /v1/estimate with endpoint "/v1/collections" first.

Collecting 500 posts with the full treatment is estimated at $194.13; budget_usd is $5.00. Lower target, raise the budget, or pass treatment "collect_only" to collect rows without judging, analysing and indexing them.

get.description: Recent collection runs for this workspace, most recent first. Each carries its status and spend; `corpus_run` is omitted here, so fetch one collection for its corpus run.

200.description: Collection runs.

get.description: Status of one collection run: collected vs target, coverage, cost so far, whether billing has settled, and why if it stopped early. Poll this after `POST /v1/collections`.

404.description: No such collection in this workspace.

post.summary: Cancel a collection run
post.description: Stops a running collection early. Billing settles for whatever landed before the cancel, never for the full budget; the settle is once-only, so a racing in-flight step cannot double-bill. Rows already collected stay in the library and remain searchable.

200.description: Cancelled (or already terminal).

404.description: No such collection in this workspace.

get.description: Status of the staged pipeline behind a full-treatment collection or a library analysis pass: which stage it is on, what each stage kept and cost, ETA, quality-gate warnings, and whether billing has settled. The same view is embedded as `corpus_run` on `GET /v1/collections/{collection_id}`, so this exists for callers that hold only the run id (for example from the webhook). Free.

200.description: The corpus run.

404.description: No such corpus run in this workspace.

post.summary: Cancel a corpus run
post.description: Stops the pipeline. A queued run is cancelled outright and the hold it carried is released. A running run finishes the stage it is on, then stops; it is billed only for the stages that completed. Rows already collected stay in the library.

200.description: Cancelled (or already terminal).

404.description: No such corpus run in this workspace.

post.summary: Create a monitor (a workflow on a schedule)
post.description:
Saves a workflow on a schedule with a hard monthly budget. `monthly_cap_usd` is required: a monitor runs unattended, so its ceiling is never optional. Price it first with `POST /v1/estimate` (`endpoint: "/v1/monitors"`), which returns the per-run cost and `monthly_expected_usd`.

Two workflows run today. `trending` re-reads the stored library each tick. `collection_topup` is the standing order that keeps a library growing: each tick starts one `/v1/collections` run per subject in `params.subjects` (1 to 10 search phrases; `params.subject` accepts a single phrase as `[subject]`; provide one or the other, not both), in array order, re-checking the remaining cap before each subject so a cap can stop the fan-out partway through (skipped subjects are attempted again next tick). Each collection uses the same `target` posts and `treatment` (full or collect_only), reserving its expected cost against the monthly cap; it settles for what actually landed (and, with the full treatment, the corpus run settles once more for the stages that ran) and the difference returns to the budget. A run whose expected cost does not fit what remains is recorded as `skipped_budget`; with `pause_at_cap` (default) the monitor pauses at the cap until the period rolls. Grow or shrink the subject list later, or change `target` or `monthly_cap_usd`, with `POST /v1/monitors/{monitor_id}/update`, with no need to recreate the schedule.

`webhook_url`, when set, receives `monitor.run.completed`: for `collection_topup` when a collection (collect_only) or its corpus run (full) has settled, with `collection_id`, `corpus_run_id`, `cost_usd` and a summary; a multi-subject tick fires one `monitor.run.completed` per subject as each of its collections settles. Deliveries are unsigned, best effort, one attempt with a 5s timeout.

params.description: `collection_topup`: exactly one of `subject` or `subjects` (required), `target` (required, 1 to 5000 per run), `platforms` (default both), `window` (default "7d"), `treatment` (default "full"). `trending`: the `/v1/trending` body.

subject.description: A single search phrase. Equivalent to `subjects: [subject]`. Provide this or `subjects`, not both.

subjects.description: 1-10 search phrases each tick fans out over, in order. Trimmed and deduped case-insensitively. Provide this or `subject`, not both.

platforms.description: Defaults to tiktok and instagram (video). Add "reddit" for text posts and comment threads: no video analysis or search index.

schedule.description: Defaults to every 24 hours. `kind` other than `daily` or `weekly` is read as `interval`.

time_utc.description: HH:MM UTC for daily/weekly. Defaults to 09:00.

monthly_cap_usd.description: Required hard ceiling per rolling 30-day period. Must cover at least one run.

webhook_url.description: Optional, `https://` on a public host. Receives `monitor.run.completed`.

daily_topup.summary: 50 posts a day on a subject, full treatment

multi_subject_topup.summary: One schedule fanning out over three search terms

estimate.description: One run of the workflow, and in `assumes` the month: `runs_per_month` and `monthly_expected_usd`.

400.description: `invalid_request`: an unsupported workflow, a missing or malformed param (the message names it), or a cap below one run's expected cost.

get.description: Every monitor in the workspace with its budget consumed, next run and, for `collection_topup`, the collection its latest run started.

200.description: The monitors.

post.summary: Pause a monitor
post.description: Pauses the monitor: no further runs are scheduled. A collection already started by its last run carries on and settles normally.

200.description: Paused.

404.description: No such monitor in this workspace.

get.summary: Get a monitor and its recent runs
get.description: The monitor plus its last 10 runs, newest first. For `collection_topup` each run carries the `collection_id` it started; a run's `cost_usd` is the reservation until that collection settles, then the actual charge.

200.description: The monitor and its runs.

404.description: No such monitor in this workspace.

post.summary: Grow or shrink a scheduled collection
post.description: Updates a `collection_topup` schedule in place: the way its search terms expand as the library grows. `add_subjects` and `remove_subjects` (by exact string) edit the subject list (removals apply before additions, so one call can swap a stale term for a fresh one without tripping the 10-subject ceiling); `target` and `monthly_cap_usd` can also change. Removing every subject is refused: pause the schedule with `POST /v1/monitors/cancel` instead. The same floor as creation applies: `monthly_cap_usd` must cover at least one run at the (possibly new) `target`. `window`, `platforms` and `treatment` are fixed for the life of a schedule; cancel and recreate for those. Returns the updated schedule in the same shape as `GET /v1/monitors/{monitor_id}`.

add_subjects.description: Search phrases to add, subject to the same 1-10 total and 500-character limits as creation. Deduped case-insensitively against what is already scheduled.

remove_subjects.description: Exact-string subjects to remove. Applied before add_subjects.

grow.summary: Add a search term the corpus should also track

swap.summary: Retire a stale term, add a fresh one

200.description: Updated.

400.description: `invalid_request`: not a `collection_topup` schedule, a malformed field, removing every subject, more than 10 subjects after adding, or a cap below one run's expected cost.

404.description: No such monitor in this workspace.

get.description:
One free read of what this workspace's library holds: how many videos, how many are analyzed, waiting or could not be analyzed, text posts, duplicates folded into their cluster, platforms, the span of posting dates, how many creators and which posted most, the formats the on-screen record shows, and the subjects recent collections were run for.

Call it before the first question: it says what the library can and cannot answer. Rows the subject judge dropped and posts from declared official accounts are withheld from every count and reported under `library.withheld`. Analysis state is decided by the same rule `POST /v1/corpus/ask` gates on, so the two never disagree about how many videos are waiting. Counts are what the library holds, not everything posted about a subject; `quality.limitations` says so, and says what else the counts cannot stand behind.

Free, and open to test keys.

200.description: The library, counted.

post.summary: Keep videos another library analyzed
post.description:
Adds videos that another Pepo library already analyzed to this one, with their analysis, transcript, on-screen record and search entry, so they can be asked about, opened and counted here. Nothing is collected and nothing is re-analyzed.

Each video actually added is one `post_collected` ($0.02). A video already in this library is reported under `already_in_library` and a video that is not analyzed anywhere under `not_available`; neither is billed. The hold is one `post_collected` per id sent, and the charge settles for the rows added.

What travels is the video and what Pepo learned from watching it. What another workspace decided about it (its subject judge's verdict, duplicate clustering, review labels, collection provenance, comments) does not: the copy starts unjudged, like a freshly collected row. Live keys only.

200.description: What was added, what was already here, and what could not be added.

post.summary: Put survey questions to the library
post.description:
Asks up to 6 questions of the library the way a survey would, each as its own `POST /v1/corpus/ask` that keeps only the videos whose answer addresses it, and reports which way those videos lean on it (favorable, unfavorable, mixed, neutral), judged from each video's own answer rather than its overall mood. A lean is only stated over 5 or more placed videos, and only as `mostly` with 60% on one side.

Each question is billed exactly as that ask: one `corpus_question`, plus one `video_read` per video whose footage is read live. An unsupported question (demographics, sales, ad spend, trending now) is refused on its own and not billed. The library gate applies once for the whole survey.

It is not a survey of people: it is what people chose to post in public, and `not_a_survey` says so on every reply.

hits.description: Videos read per question, and the per-question price ceiling.

200.description: Each question's answer and lean, or the library gate.

reason.description: Present only when the library gate held the survey back; `questions` is then empty.

post.summary: What the outperforming videos have in common
post.description:
Measures each video against its own creator's median views in this library, calls a video at 2x that median or more an outperformer, and compares outperformers with the other comparable videos on the on-screen record (format, setting, who is on screen, whether the creator is on camera, mood), length and platform. Returns the strongest outperformers with their hooks, to draw ideas from.

Measuring within each creator keeps a large account's ordinary video from reading as a hit. Views are one observation at collection time, so videos under 3 days old are left out; creators with fewer than 3 videos here have no median and are left out. Below 8 analyzed videos on either side, `comparison` is null and `withheld_because` says why: a pattern across a handful of videos is not ranked. It shows association, not cause.

Read and billed like the other reports over the stored library: one `search_request` plus one `content_enriched` per video read.

term.description: Only videos whose caption, summary or themes mention this.

200.description: The comparison, or why there is none.

bearerAuth.description:
A workspace-scoped API key: `Authorization: Bearer pk_live_...`.

The workspace is derived from the key. **No endpoint accepts a brand or tenant identifier**, and none ever will: an identifier that travels through a language model is a cross-tenant leak waiting for a prompt injection. `X-Api-Key` is accepted as an alternative header for hosts that cannot set `Authorization`.

Cost.description: What this request cost, in USD.

Balance.description: Remaining workspace balance after this request, in USD.

RequestId.description: Send this back to us when reporting a problem.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, malformed or revoked key. All three are reported identically so a probing client learns nothing from the difference.

InsufficientCredits.description: The request would exceed the workspace balance, so no work was started and nothing was charged. The error carries cheaper plans that do fit: an error that says only "no" ends an agent's task.

error.message: This request is estimated at $5.00. The workspace balance is $4.93, with $4.12 currently available to spend.

ProfileRequired.description: No approved brand profile for this workspace. Results would be generic category noise rather than answers about this brand, so the call is refused with the path to fix it.

error.message: This workspace has no approved brand profile. Every workflow reads it, so results would be generic category noise rather than answers about your brand.

InvalidRequest.description: A parameter was malformed, or the body carried a field this endpoint does not accept (unknown fields are refused rather than ignored). Nothing was charged. `field` names the offender when one parameter is at fault.

error.message: Could not parse window "7dd". Use a number followed by h or d, e.g. "24h" or "7d", or "all".

TestKeyReadOnly.description: This request was made with a `pk_test_` key. Test keys are read-only: this call writes to the workspace or spends provider credits, so it requires a live key.

error.message: This is a test key, and test keys are read-only. A collection calls a paid provider, so start it with a live key.

ProviderUnavailable.description: A provider this endpoint depends on is not configured on this deployment. A Pepo-side configuration problem, not a problem with the request: nothing is reserved or charged, the balance is untouched, and retrying will not help until the named setting exists. `provider` names the provider and `missing_config` the setting.

error.message: This deployment has no TwelveLabs credential, so the indexed footage cannot be read. Nothing was charged.

RateLimited.description: Test keys only. A `pk_test_` key is limited to a fixed number of requests per minute on the metered endpoints, because it never meters and a request limit is the only thing bounding it. No `Retry-After` header is sent: `reset_at` (unix ms) says when the window resets. Live keys are never rate limited here.

error.message: This test key is limited to 30 requests per minute. Test keys never meter, so a request limit is the only thing bounding them. Try again in 12s.

Usage.description: The meter, returned with every metered response. You cannot see a dashboard from inside an agent, so the meter travels with the payload. The work always runs to completion; a ceiling limits the charge, never the result.

cost_usd.description: What this request was actually charged.

balance_usd.description: Workspace balance after this request. `0` on a test key, which has no balance.

billed.description: Per-unit detail of what the work metered, including candidates read but not returned. When `charge_capped` is true these lines sum to `metered_usd`, not to `cost_usd`.

unit.description: The billing unit. The full list and prices are on the credits page; not every unit appears on every endpoint.

charge_capped.description: True when the metered cost went above the amount held for this call (the smaller of the estimate and `max_cost_usd` or the server default), so the charge stopped at the hold. **Results are complete either way**: every workflow runs to completion before it is billed, and a capped call returns exactly what an uncapped one would.

metered_usd.description: What the `billed` lines add up to before any cap. Equal to `cost_usd` unless `charge_capped` is true. On a test key, what the work would have cost on a live key.

truncated.description: Deprecated alias of `charge_capped`, always the same value. It never meant partial results: results are complete. Read `charge_capped` instead.

unmetered.description: Present only on a test-key response: nothing was charged, and `metered_usd` is what the work would have cost.

Coverage.description: How much observation is behind a score. Read this before the score.

metrics_missing.description: When a platform does not expose a metric, the remaining ones are reweighted and `confidence` is lowered.

Momentum.description: A score is never returned alone.

classification.description: `trending` requires top-decile rank in the comparison group, at least 1.5x the creator's own baseline, and growth across consecutive snapshots. `breakout` requires top 2%, 3x baseline, and still accelerating.

n.description: How many comparable videos this was ranked against. A small `n` makes any percentile weak, which is why it is returned rather than hidden.

floors_met.description: Whether the evidence bar for this claim was actually cleared.

gated_by.description: Present when the classification was capped below what the score alone would suggest. **Do not describe a gated result as trending.**
gated_by.example: Capped at watchlist: 2 spaced observation(s) over 3h. "trending" requires at least 3 across 12h.

components.description: Component values, `null` where not computable. Percentiles are within the comparison group, never raw rates.

creatorBaselineLift.description: Multiple of the creator's own normal performance. 1.0 is exactly normal.

analysis.description: The video's own stored analysis, when a response includes one. Not a number this run computed. Absent (or null) means either no analysis is stored, or this endpoint does not attach one.

pilotEvidence.description: Returned by `POST /v1/search/videos` and `GET /v1/videos/{video_id}` (null when the row carries none). Not returned by trending.

Metrics.description: Absent values are `null`, never `0`. A metric that was never observed is a different fact from a metric observed at zero.

VideoAnalysis.description: The video's stored analysis: what it says, and what it shows. Null when no analysis is stored, which is not the same as an analysis that found nothing, and is reported as its own state rather than as empty fields.

hook.description: The opening line or opening image, verbatim.

kind.description: claim | complaint | request | question, as classified by the analysis pass. Null when the stored record carries none.

about.description: The entity the claim concerns, or null when general.

sentiment.description: Overall valence the creator expressed toward the main thing the video is about (positive | negative | mixed | neutral | not_determinable). Null when no analysis is stored.

entities.description: Every brand, product, person or organization the analysis found substantively discussed, with the creator's stance toward each read from this video alone.

stance_evidence.description: The quoted words, on-screen text, or described image the stance was read from.

onScreen.description: What the video shows. Null for a video analyzed before the on-screen record existed.

trend.description: The cluster-level verdict, reported separately from the ranking.

verdict.description: `emerging_trend` needs at least 5 accelerating videos from 3 independent creators. `confirmed_trend` needs 15 videos from 8 creators, top-5% cluster velocity, and no single creator holding more than 50% of the cluster's views. `cannot_tell` means no video in the cluster has an acceleration measurement, which takes three metric snapshots (most often a frozen archive with none), so acceleration could not be measured. It is not the same as `not_a_trend`, which means videos were measured and found flat: report `cannot_tell` as unknown, never as evidence the subject is not trending.

posts_trend_grade.description: How many posts have enough observation history to be classified beyond `watchlist`.

excluded_by_brand_profile.description: Results withheld by the brand profile's exclusion list.

excluded_by_judge.description: Results withheld because the corpus judge (the subject-collision check every collected row goes through) explicitly marked them off-subject. Never included in this count when it merely was not judged yet.

excluded_official.description: Results withheld because the author is a declared official account (`official_accounts` on the brand profile); this brand's own or a competitor's. Withheld for both: a subject's own post about itself is not someone else's voice.

caveat.description: A plain-language statement when the corpus cannot support the question asked: an empty corpus, no metric history, or too little history to classify anything. Pass it on verbatim.
caveat.example: No metric history exists yet for this workspace, so nothing can be scored for momentum.

brand_profile_version.description: Which profile version produced these results. Two runs against different versions are not comparable.

disclaimer.description: Ships on every response carrying view-derived numbers.
disclaimer.example: Views are observed content views (potential exposures), not ad impressions. Ad impressions require first-party or Ads Manager data.

adoption.description: How many distinct creators adopted this over time. A view count says how far a few videos travelled; adoption says whether anything spread. A creator is counted once, at their first post, so a prolific account is one adopter rather than a movement.

bucket_hours.description: Bucket width. Fixed per window so two analyses of the same window are comparable.

top_creator_share.description: Share of videos from the single busiest creator, 0-1. Travels with the series so a rising line cannot be quoted without it.

summary.description: One-line reading of the curve, safe to restate verbatim.

new_creators.description: Creators posting for the first time in this bucket: the adopters.

axes.description: Comparative bars for hooks, formats and topics. An axis is null when too little of the corpus could be classified.

medianViews.description: Median views for this bucket. The most common bucket is routinely the worst performing, so a count alone answers the wrong question.

unclassified.description: Videos this axis could not classify. Reported rather than hidden.

medianViews.description: Median views for this bucket. The most common bucket is routinely the worst performing, so a count alone answers the wrong question.

unclassified.description: Videos this axis could not classify. Reported rather than hidden.

medianViews.description: Median views for this bucket. The most common bucket is routinely the worst performing, so a count alone answers the wrong question.

unclassified.description: Videos this axis could not classify. Reported rather than hidden.

withheld.description: Axes not returned, each with the reason. Includes 'sounds', which no collected field supports.

actions.description: Next steps, with arguments pre-filled. Actions that are not implemented appear in `unavailable` with a reason: never offered, never silently omitted.

args.description: Pass straight through to the named tool.

reason.description: Why it cannot be offered. Shown so a gap is explained rather than discovered.

test_mode.description: Present only when the request used a `pk_test_` key: nothing was charged and no collection ran. A statement about billing, not about the data.

test_mode_notice.description: Present with `test_mode`. A sentence to show a person.

demo.description: Present only when this workspace is a Pepo demo workspace: the videos, creators and competitors are sample data, not the caller's brand. A property of the workspace, not of the key.

demo_notice.description: Present with `demo`. Pass it on so sample data is never read as the caller's own.

matched_on.description: `analysis`: the match was in the video's stored analysis (summary, hook, themes, claim text) rather than its caption or handle. `pilot_evidence`: the match was in reviewed pilot identity evidence (brand and product family).

excluded_by_judge.description: Results withheld because the corpus judge (the subject-collision check every collected row goes through) explicitly marked them off-subject. Never included in this count when it merely was not judged yet.

excluded_official.description: Results withheld because the author is a declared official account (`official_accounts` on the brand profile); this brand's own or a competitor's. Withheld for both: a subject's own post about itself is not someone else's voice.

search_method.description: **Read this.** States exactly which fields were searched, so an empty result is not mistaken for an absence of such video.
search_method.example: Token overlap over stored captions, creator handles, each video's stored analysis (summary, hook, themes, claims) when one has been run, and reviewed product-family identity when present. Versioned pilot rows require every query term to match, so a generic family word cannot substitute for a specific product noun. Raw transcripts, on-screen text, detected products/logos and audio are NOT searched because those fields are not present in this corpus yet, so an empty result is not evidence that no such video exists.

answer.description: The answer, one paragraph per cited video. Each paragraph ends on its own line with the citation: `@handle`, then an em dash (U+2014), then the video URL, then the best matching clip as `(m:ss` en dash (U+2013) `m:ss)`. A video with no known creator is cited as `(unknown creator)`. Null when `reason` is set.

reason.description: `no_index`: nothing indexed for this workspace yet (unbilled). `no_hits`: no indexed video matched within the window (billed one `corpus_question`). `unsupported_question`: the question asks for something no video could ever answer (audience demographics, sales or revenue, ad spend, or whether something is trending now, which is `POST /v1/trending`), decided before any search or read (unbilled). `needs_analysis`: some videos in the library (inside `window`, when one was given) have not been analyzed yet (unbilled); `library` carries the counts and, when nothing is already running, `estimated_cost_usd`; call `POST /v1/library/analyze` to start it. `analysis_running`: the same gate, but a pass is already running for this brand; `library.analysis_in_progress` names it, check it with `GET /v1/collections/{collection_id}` and ask again once it finishes.

post_id.description: Usable with `GET /v1/videos/{video_id}` and `video_ids` when the video is in this library.

start_s.description: Best matching clip, seconds from the start of the video.

in_your_library.description: Present when `libraries` is `all`: false for a video only another library holds. Keep it with `POST /v1/library/add`; until then `GET /v1/videos/{video_id}` and `video_ids` cannot read it.

hits_considered.description: Videos actually read for the answer (at most `hits`).

index_videos.description: Videos in this workspace's index, one per duplicate cluster, so smaller than the library. Null for `unsupported_question`, `needs_analysis` and `analysis_running`, which are decided before the index is checked.

library.description: Present only when reason is `needs_analysis` or `analysis_running`.

indexes_searched.description: How many of this workspace's video indexes were searched. A large library is split across several indexes, and every one of them is searched.

indexes_unavailable.description: Indexes that could not be searched (deleted, or the provider errored). Non-null only when that happened. Their videos are missing from this answer, so read it as thinner than the corpus by that much rather than as a complete result.

degraded.description: Provider-thinned coverage among the cited hits. Present only when at least one hit fell back or went unanswered because the video provider returned HTTP 429, a live read or its asset lookup ran out of time (`provider_timeout`), the shared read-capacity wait expired, or a held read lease was lost.

asked.description: The request echoed back, so a null answer is actionable. `window` is the caller's own filter: `no_hits` with a window set means "nothing in that period", not "nothing in this corpus", and widening it is usually the fix.

video_ids.description: The videos the ask was scoped to, or null for the whole library.

cached.description: Present only when this answer came from the answer cache: produced earlier by `method` for the same video and the same question, with no provider call and no read billed this time.

retrieval.description: How this hit was found. `index`: a plain footage-index match (the default, so it is omitted rather than sent). `analysis`: the re-rank picked it from the stored analyses and the footage index did not surface it. `both`: the footage index matched it too.

used_on_screen.description: Present only on a `read_transcript` answer that relied on the video's stored on-screen record (a visual detail the transcript does not state), whether or not a transcript quote backs it too.

sources.description: How each cited video was answered: from its stored timed transcript and on-screen record by a text model (`read_transcript`, tried first), read live from the footage (`read_footage`, only when the stored text cannot answer), from the stored analysis (`stored_analysis`), or not at all (`unanswered`). `cached: true` means the answer was served from an earlier identical question about the same video with no provider call. Only an uncached `read_footage` source is billed, as one `video_read`. `degraded_reason` is present only when that hit was thinned by a provider 429, a provider timeout, a shared read-capacity timeout, or a lost shared read lease.

rerank.description: Whether the analysis re-rank ran before the footage index was searched: a text-model pass over the stored analyses (sentiment, hook, summary, themes, claims) that surfaces videos a footage search can miss, for example a "what are people complaining about" question landing on videos whose analysis carries a `complaint` claim. Null when the ask never reached the index.

picked.description: How many of the final hits came from the re-rank's own picks, before the answer was cut to `hits`.

skipped.description: Present only when the re-rank did not run to completion, in which case the answer is exactly what it would have been without this feature. Absent means it ran, even if it picked nothing worth moving to the front.

search_method.description: **Read this.** States what was searched. Only analyzed, indexed videos are read, one per duplicate cluster; captions are not searched here.

test_mode_notice.description: Present with `test_mode`. A sentence to show a person.

first_asked_at.description: Unix ms of the oldest question in this group within the window, or null when the group is empty.

last_asked_at.description: Unix ms of the newest question in this group within the window, or null when the group is empty.

questions.description: Newest first, capped at 50: enough to act on, not the whole window.

source.description: Which endpoint logged it: `ask_corpus` is `POST /v1/corpus/ask`, `search_videos` is `POST /v1/search/videos`.

result_count.description: `hits_considered` (ask) or `matched` (search) at the time this question was logged.

brand_own.description: True when the brand itself posted this video. A brand's own posts are never counted as signal by the workflow endpoints; null when unknown.

excluded.description: True when the subject check marked this video off-subject (or pilot evidence marked it ineligible). Excluded videos are withheld from every other read; this endpoint still returns one by id so it can be audited.

media.description: The playable file, when one was captured. `video_url_kind` says which of two different things `video_url` is: `stored` is a durable copy Pepo holds and can be played whenever, `cdn_signed` is the **signed platform url captured at ingest, which expires within hours**: treat that one as best-effort and fall back to `video.thumb_url` and `video.url`. Null on rows with neither, and on platforms that serve no direct file.

mime.description: Content type of the stored copy. Present only when `video_url_kind` is `stored`.

bytes.description: Size of the stored copy in bytes. Present only when `video_url_kind` is `stored`.

history.description: The observation series behind any momentum claim about this video: the evidence, not the conclusion.

unknown.description: Comments carrying no classification. Never folded into `neutral`: guessing would inflate the coverage number, which is the one figure meant to be trustworthy.

author.description: Handle, or the display name when no handle was captured.

author_handle.description: The handle alone. Null rather than the display name, so a client rendering `@` + this value never prints `@Jane Doe`.

evidence_note.description: States what grounding this video's analysis does and does not have.
evidence_note.example: Timestamped visual/spoken evidence is not stored for this video.

disclaimer.description: Ships on every response carrying view-derived numbers.
disclaimer.example: Views are observed content views (potential exposures), not ad impressions.

lens.description: This workspace's industry vocabulary: which words every tool and report uses for "product", "competitor", "SKU", "review" and "consumer". Inferred from `category` when omitted (music/label/artist/band/record → `music`, else `cpg`).

judge_category.description: What counts as on-topic vs. noise when the corpus judge reads collected posts for this brand. Different from `category` (the industry label): this refines the judge's category definition. The judge never sees the brand name itself, so phrase `means`/`other` about the content, not the brand.

means.description: What on-topic content is for this brand, when judging collected posts.

other.description: What should be treated as noise, when judging collected posts.

exclusions.description: Topics this brand refuses to be associated with. Enforced server-side in every workflow: matching results are withheld and counted in `corpus.excluded_by_brand_profile`.

platform.description: Omit to match this handle on any platform.

owner.description: Must name an entry already in `brand_names` or `competitors` on this same profile, or it rides back in `official_account_gaps`.

official_accounts.description: This brand's and its competitors' own accounts. A post from one of these is withheld at read time from search, trending, share of voice, product and competitor results, as the subject talking, never as conversation about it, and counted in `excluded_official`.

official_account_gaps.description: One message per declared `official_accounts` entry whose `owner` matches neither `brand_names` nor `competitors`. Recomputed on every read, not just at write time.

estimated_cost_usd.description: What the refused call would have cost. Nothing was charged.

balance_usd.description: The workspace's actual balance, matching GET /v1/credits. Some of it may already be tied up in other active holds.

available_balance_usd.description: What is currently spendable after subtracting other active holds from the actual balance.

suggestions.description: Computed against your actual balance. The first entry is the largest version of your request that still fits.

field.description: Which parameter was malformed. Present whenever one parameter is at fault; absent when the whole body was (for example, not a JSON object).

provider.description: The third-party provider this endpoint needs and cannot reach.

missing_config.description: The deployment setting whose absence caused this, named so the person who can fix it does not have to guess which provider key is missing.

view_share.description: Share of ATTRIBUTED views, not of the whole corpus.

summary.description: One line a client can restate. Leads with the refusal when the split is not quotable.

reliable.description: Deprecated: prefer `reliability`. True only when `reliability` is `"reliable"`. Previously also came back true for a corpus of unrecorded origin (`reliability: "directional"`), which is why it is being replaced: a client checking only this boolean quoted a directional split as solid.

reliability.description: **Check this before quoting any percentage.** `unreliable`: the corpus cannot support a share number at all: report `reliability_because` instead of the split, never a number. `directional`: how the corpus was gathered is not confirmed as category-level: a percentage may be quoted but only labelled directional/approximate. `reliable`: quote the split as-is.

reliability_because.description: The one reason behind `reliability`, restatable verbatim.

corpus_origin.description: How the corpus was gathered, derived from the collection runs behind it rather than supplied by the caller.

setup_gaps.description: Configuration problems (no brand names, no competitors) that prevent a share of voice. Distinct from a data problem: the fix is different.

comparisons.description: Videos naming both the brand and a competitor. Counted for neither side.

unattributed.description: Videos naming no brand at all.

window_hours.description: Hours the read covered; null when it covered all time (no `window`, or `all`).

excluded_official.description: Results withheld because the author is a declared official account (`official_accounts` on the brand profile); this brand's own or a competitor's. Withheld for both: a subject's own post about itself is not someone else's voice.

reconciles.description: The rows sum exactly to `delta`. Computed, not assumed. If false the breakdown is defective and must not be presented.
