Collection.description: A collection run, as returned by every /v1/collections endpoint. `reason` is set when the run stopped for something other than reaching `target`: a cancel, a settle, or an error.

collected.description: Videos landed in the library so far. This is what is billed.

coverage.description: Coverage of the collected set against the request. Shape varies by run.

cost_usd.description: Spend so far. Not final until `settled` is true.

settled.description: Whether billing has settled for what actually landed. False while the run is still going.

treatment.description: `full`: a corpus run follows collection. `collect_only`: rows only. A run recorded before treatments existed reads as `collect_only`.

corpus_run.description: The corpus run behind a full-treatment collection, once enqueued. Null before that and for `collect_only`. Omitted from `GET /v1/collections`, which does not look runs up.

finished_at.description: Unix ms, or null while still running.

monitor_id.description: Set when a scheduled collection (a `collection_topup` monitor) started this run.

scanned.description: Every provider item the run paged through, including duplicates and out-of-window drops. Not billed.

estimated_cost_usd.description: What this run is estimated to cost. Nothing was started or charged.

budget_usd.description: The `budget_usd` you sent. Absent when the workspace call cap, not the budget, fell short.

field.description: Present when `budget_usd` itself was below the estimate.

held_usd.description: Present when the workspace's default call cap, not `budget_usd`, is what fell short of the estimate.

CorpusRunStage.description: One stage of a corpus run, in pipeline order. `output` is the quantity billed at the stage's unit (judge → dataset_row_verified, enrich → content_enriched, analyze → video_analyzed, index → video_indexed, comments → comment_collected, sentiment → comment_judged; dedup is free).

label.description: Short plain-language name for this step, for showing to a person (e.g. `subject check`). Render this rather than mapping `name` yourself.

description.description: What this step is doing, as a sentence (e.g. `checking each video is really about this subject`).

note.description: Human line, e.g. "34 kept, 6 excluded as off-subject". Quality-gate warnings start with "warning".

CorpusRun.description: The staged pipeline a full-treatment collection hands its rows to. Settles once, at the end, with one billed line per stage that produced output; `charge_capped` means the stages metered more than the hold the collection left and the charge stopped at the hold. `warnings` are the quality gates that fired (too few rows kept by judge, too many collapsed by dedup). The run continues; the operator decides whether to cancel.

attempt.description: How many times a worker has claimed the run. A run whose worker goes quiet is re-queued; the third stale claim fails it.

current_stage_label.description: Plain-language name for `current_stage`, or null when no step is running.

cost_usd.description: Stage spend. Final once `settled` is true.

eta_minutes.description: Remaining stages × the measured per-stage time of this run; null until a stage has finished, and once the run is over.

Monitor.description: A saved workflow on a schedule with a hard monthly budget: the only thing in this API that spends money with no human present. Spend is tracked per rolling 30-day period; a run whose expected cost does not fit what remains is recorded as `skipped_budget`, and with `pause_at_cap` the monitor flips to `capped` until the period rolls or the cap is raised.

workflow.description: `trending` re-reads the stored corpus each run. `collection_topup` starts one `/v1/collections` run per subject in `params.subjects` each tick: the standing order that keeps a corpus current, and grows to more search terms over time via `POST /v1/monitors/{id}/update`.

params.description: For `collection_topup`: `{subjects, platforms, window, target, treatment}`, normalised: `subjects` is always an array here (1 or more entries), even when the schedule was created with a single `subject`. For `trending`: the `/v1/trending` body.

monthly_cap_usd.description: The hard ceiling per rolling 30-day period.

spent_this_period_usd.description: For `collection_topup` this includes the reservation of any run still in flight; it is corrected to the actual charge when the collection settles.

last_collection_id.description: `collection_topup` only: the collection the latest run started. Poll it on `GET /v1/collections/{collection_id}`.

MonitorRun.description: One execution of a monitor. Skipped runs are recorded too: a monitor that silently stops is indistinguishable from a broken one.

cost_usd.description: For `collection_topup`: the reservation while the collection is in flight (`summary.accounting: "reserved"`), the actual charge once it settled (`"settled"`).

collection_id.description: `collection_topup` only: the collection this run started.

LibraryStatus.description: Where this workspace's library stands on analysis: watched and searchable, still waiting, or given up on. Read from POST /v1/corpus/ask when reason is needs_analysis or analysis_running, and from POST /v1/library/analyze.

videos_waiting_for_analysis.description: Could be watched, has not been yet. This is what blocks POST /v1/corpus/ask until it reaches zero, inside the asked window.

videos_that_could_not_be_analyzed.description: Tried and failed, or had nothing to fetch. Reported, never blocking: a video that will never download must not hold every answer hostage.

videos_of_unknown_length.description: A subset of videos_waiting_for_analysis, not an addition to it: nobody has measured these yet. Longer videos are billed per length rather than a single flat price, and an unmeasured video is priced as a short one until it is; the actual charge never goes above the amount held when the analysis starts.

estimated_cost_usd.description: What analyzing the waiting videos is estimated to cost, priced per step each one still needs, and by length past 3 minutes. On `POST /v1/library/analyze` it is the estimate for this pass only. Absent on a `/v1/corpus/ask` answer while a pass is already running.

analysis_in_progress.description: The run already catching this library up, when one is running. Check it with GET /v1/collections/{collection_id}.

estimated_cost_usd.description: With `field`: what analyzing the first waiting video is estimated to cost. With `held_usd`: what this pass is estimated to cost. Nothing was started or charged.

field.description: Present when max_cost_usd itself was below the estimate.

held_usd.description: Present when the workspace's own call cap, not max_cost_usd, is what fell short of the estimate.

reset_at.description: Unix ms when this key's request window resets.

message.description: Carries the provider's own error text, verbatim.

PilotEvidence.description: Curated identity evidence imported for a pilot workspace, reported separately from the video's own analysis. Null on every row that carries none, which is nearly every row. `caption_mention` is not proof a product is depicted, and `reviewed_family` is provisional AI review, not human or catalog verification. Rows whose status is `unknown`, `rejected` or `conflicted` are not eligible and are withheld from evidence.

policyVersion.description: The eligibility policy the importer applied.

snapshotDate.description: Date of the source archive snapshot. Metrics were not independently rechecked at that time.

targetContext.description: `parent_post_only`: the evidence is about the parent post, not the row it is attached to.

OnScreen.description: What the video SHOWS, recorded once when it was analyzed, separately from what is said. The facets are closed vocabularies so many videos can be counted against each other; the free text is short and timed so it can be quoted. Null for a video analyzed before this record existed, which is not the same as a video that shows nothing.

mood.description: The tone the visuals and delivery convey.

actions.description: What people are visibly doing, as short verb phrases.

productsShown.description: Products the video features, or whose brand is legible on screen.

brand.description: As it appears on the product or packaging. Empty string when none is legible.

startTime.description: Seconds from the start when it first appears.

onScreenText.description: Titles, overlays, prices, labels and signs, copied exactly.

scenes.description: The timed visual log, in order.

AcrossVideos.description: Deterministic counts over the cited videos' stored sentiment and on-screen records, so a comparison is built on numbers rather than tallied by eye from the paragraphs. No model judgment. Present only when at least two videos were cited. Each list is sorted by count and holds at most 8 rows.

with_on_screen.description: How many of them have an on-screen record. The on-screen counts below are out of this number, never out of `videos`.

videos.description: Videos with this value. Each video counts once per value.

sentiment.description: The creator's overall valence, from each video's stored analysis.

videos.description: Videos with this value. Each video counts once per value.

product_shown_how.description: How products appear (held, applied, packaging...), counted per video.

videos.description: Videos with this value. Each video counts once per value.

brands_shown.description: Brands legible on screen, counted per video. Spellings that differ only in case, spaces or punctuation count as one brand.

videos.description: Videos with this value. Each video counts once per value.

products.description: Product types counted per video, from a product-type mapping when one was made, otherwise from folded exact product names.

videos.description: Videos with this value. Each video counts once per value.

recurring_actions.description: Visible actions that recur in more than one video.

RecordRow.description: One row of the library as stored. Fields the platform never supplied are omitted rather than zero.

views.description: Observed content views, never ad impressions.

skus.description: Brand-profile products whose name appears in the caption.

sentiment.description: The video's overall valence from its stored analysis. Null when the video has not been analyzed.

judgeExcluded.description: True when the subject check (or pilot evidence) excluded the row. Only ever true when `include_excluded=true` let it through.

sample.description: Every post the provider returned, in page order. Nothing is saved.

views.description: Observed content views, never ad impressions.

mention_subject.description: Share of those posts, 0 to 1, whose caption names the subject. 0 when the page was empty.

mention_rate.description: Share of all returned posts, 0 to 1, whose caption names the subject.

suggestion.description: A sentence to show a person: what to try when the subject is matching something else.

label.description: What the step does, in words a person reads.

tool.description: The MCP tool that performs it. Each maps to an endpoint here: `ask_library` is `POST /v1/corpus/ask`, `get_video` is `GET /v1/videos/{video_id}`, `library_overview` is `GET /v1/library`, `analyze_library` is `POST /v1/library/analyze`, `get_collection` is `GET /v1/collections/{collection_id}`.

args.description: Arguments filled in, to pass straight through. A follow-up question is left for the caller to write.

ActionSet.description: What the result offers next. A step that is not wired is listed under `unavailable` with its reason, never silently left out.

videos.description: Videos that count: analyzed, waiting and could not be analyzed.

waiting_for_analysis.description: Not analyzed yet. An ask over them returns `needs_analysis` until they are.

text_posts.description: Reddit and other text posts: in the library, never analyzed as video.

duplicates_folded.description: Copies folded into their duplicate cluster's representative.

most_videos.description: Creators with the most videos in this library. A count of what was collected, not of what they post or how they perform.

subjects.description: Recent collections' subjects, newest first. Library analysis passes and imports are left out.

post_id.description: The video's id in this library.

answer.description: One paragraph per answering video, each with its citation, as on `POST /v1/corpus/ask`.

videos_answering.description: Videos the addressing judge said address the question. Only these are counted, leaned and quoted.

videos_unjudged.description: Videos kept whose addressing could not be judged (the judge timed out or failed). They are not counted in `lean` and not quoted.

indexes_unavailable.description: Indexes that could not be searched. Non-null means a partial result, and `caveat` says so.

degraded.description: Present when some reads fell back (provider limits, timeouts, shared capacity).

lean.description: How the answering videos lean on this question's own subject, judged from each video's answer, not its overall mood.

leans.description: Null under 5 placed videos. `mostly` needs 60% of them on one side; otherwise `divided`.

says.description: What this video's own answer says about the question. Only lines in quotation marks are verbatim transcript; the rest is the model's reading of the video.

across_videos.description: As on `POST /v1/corpus/ask`, over the answering videos.

outperformer_share.description: Percent of that side's videos with a known value.

others_share.description: Percent of that side's videos with a known value.

difference_points.description: Percentage points; positive means more common among outperformers.

videos_read.description: Videos read after the window, platform and term filters. Billed as `content_enriched`.

outperformers.description: Videos at 2x or more of their own creator's median views in this library.

too_recent.description: Under 3 days old: views still climbing.

no_creator.description: No creator handle, so no creator median to measure against.

no_posted_date.description: No posting date, so its age cannot be checked.

creator_has_too_few_videos.description: From creators with fewer than 3 videos here, so no median to measure against.

quality.description: The comparison reads only videos with an on-screen record: how many of each side that is, and how many comparable videos are not in the shares.

comparison.description: Per attribute (format, setting, people_on_screen, creator_on_camera, mood, length, platform), each value's share among outperformers against the other comparable videos, most over-represented first. Null when either side has fewer than 8 analyzed videos: `withheld_because` says so.

outperformers_known.description: Outperformers with this attribute known: the denominator of outperformer_share.

others_known.description: Other videos with this attribute known: the denominator of others_share.

examples.description: The strongest outperformers against their own creator, with hooks, to draw ideas from.
